newsitem.title: UK: TR Pacific sees NE Asia outperforming.
newsitem.headline: TR Pacific sees NE Asia outperforming.

text.p: TR Pacific Investment Trust said on Tuesday it expected North East Asian stocks to continue to make the running in the Far East, but anticipated strong gains in other parts of the region next year as the economic outlook improves.

"Shares in the Far East are cheap by both historic and global standards and uncertainties over currencies will give rise to attractive investment opportunities," said TR Pacific Chairman Iain Dale in a release accompanying interim results.
He said a recent substantial currency adjustment in Thailand and related weakness in other currencies now cleared the decks for confidence to be restored.
The 251 million sterling trust said performances in the six months to June 30 showed wide discrepancies between stock markets in North East Asia and those in South East Asia.

"This reflected an improving economic outlook for North East Asia following earlier slow growth, against heightened uncertainty throughout ASEAN countries as economic difficulties in Thailand unsettled sentiment."
TR Pacific, which plans to change its name to Henderson TR Pacific Investment Trust plc, posted a 12 percent rise in net asset value per share to 123 pence over the six month period.
It said it had a strong belief in long term gearing with most of a five-year $30m loan taken out last March invested.
"The board believes strongly in the benefits of long term gearing. Over time we would expect to comfortably exceed borrowing costs by investing in the region's stock markets," Dale said.

Far East stock markets posted a sterling adjusted rise of three percent for the first six months of 1997 in the MSCI Far East (ex Japan) Free Index. Over the twelve months to June, the index fell by 5.8 percent in sterling terms while TR Pacific's NAV rose by 4.0.
At end-June, the trust's biggest weighting was in Hong Kong with 29 percent, followed by Taiwan with 18.7 percent, Indonesia with 11.9 percent and Singapore with 11.3 percent.
The best performers in sterling terms over the period were Taiwan with 32.5 percent, Hong Kong with 16 percent and Indonesia with 13.6 percent.
